messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@vendr.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Whistic -> Vendr profile migration: escrowed evidence + temporary creds choreography

Hi Emily and Karthik,

We're preparing to migrate Clearstream's security profile out of Whistic and into Vendr by the end of Q2. The two items Security asked us to validate before cutover: (1) an evidence staging approach that doesn't require vendors to share long-lived objects (we prefer ephemeral upload tokens into a controlled S3 staging bucket), and (2) a short attestation that Vendr will preserve hashed proofs of possession for our SOC 2 evidence (audit trail + immutable checksum).

Attached is a proposed migration plan (redwood-vendr-migration-plan.xlsx) with a suggested canary window and rollback steps. Can you confirm if Vendr supports short-lived pre-signed POSTs for uploads and whether you can provide:
- a test presign endpoint we can hit from our validation harness,
- an S3 ingest flow that writes an audit event to our audit topic (or forwards logs), and
- a simple attestation we can sign via DocuSign to confirm evidence possession for SOC2 reference?

Timing: proposal is to run a canary on 2026-07-02 and full migration on 2026-07-06. If any of this requires additional security review, loop Priya and Ben.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Security Program Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@vendr.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: vendor-platform@vendr.com
Date: 2026-06-28T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Whistic -> Vendr profile migration: escrowed evidence + temporary creds choreography

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the plan and the XLSX — this is doable. Summary of what we can provide out of the box:
- Pre-signed POSTs (short-lived, default TTL 15 minutes) via our staging API; we can expose a test presign endpoint: https://vendr-staging-api.vendr.com/test-presign (see attached vendr-s3-temporary-credentials-guide.pdf).
- We can configure the ingest path to call a webhook on success; if you prefer we can forward CloudTrail-like events to an S3 audit bucket or push to your audit topic (we'll need a delivery endpoint).
- For SOC 2 evidence possession: we can produce a signed manifest (SHA256 checksums) per upload and store a timestamped hash chain. If Redwood requires a formal attestation, we can sign a short statement in DocuSign.

One question: are you expecting vendor-managed KMS for the upload flow, or will Redwood generate the presign tokens from a Redwood-side service? Both are possible but have different audit/PKI implications.

I can get you the presign endpoint and a DocuSign envelope by EOD.

—Emily
Emily Zhao
Platform Partnerships | Vendr
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@vendr.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-28T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Whistic -> Vendr profile migration: escrowed evidence + temporary creds choreography

Emily — appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifying points (internal + for vendor):

- Preferred flow: Redwood will mint presign tokens via its own service (we want tokens derived from our KMS so we can revoke if needed). That means Vendr needs to accept uploads signed with our presigns and surface the manifest/hash back to us.
- TTL: 15 minutes is fine for the canary; for large bulk shipments we may need to increase to 30 minutes but want to avoid >1hr.
- Audit forwarding: Priya, Ben — please confirm if forwarding to our audit S3 bucket with object-copy-event metadata is acceptable for the compliance reviewers. If not, we need a fallback to webhook + CloudWatch events.

Emily — can you drop the staging presign endpoint and a sample manifest response schema (even as a curl example) into the Jira ticket SEC-874 so Priya can review?

Thanks,
Karthik
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@vendr.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-28T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Whistic -> Vendr profile migration: escrowed evidence + temporary creds choreography

Karthik / Mina,

This approach looks acceptable from a control perspective with these conditions:
1) Presigned tokens must be generated from Redwood's KMS-backed service (so we retain revocation control).
2) Vendr must surface a manifest with SHA256 checksums and a signed timestamp for each batch; manifests should be written to the staging bucket and retained immutable for 90 days (read-only).
3) All upload and manifest actions must emit audit events (requester IP, token id, object key, timestamp) that are accessible to Redwood (webhook or S3 event replication).
4) Before full cutover, Vendr must sign a short attestation confirming evidence possession custody for Clearstream's SOC 2 reference. Please provide a DocuSign envelope for the attestation.

If Vendr can confirm these items we approve the canary on 2026-07-02. Ben — can you own the canary validation runbook? I'll review the attestation language once it's in DocuSign.

-Priya
Priya Natarajan
Security Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — confirmable. Actions we've completed:
- DocuSign attestation created and sent: https://app.docusign.com/REDACTED/EnvelopeId=abc123 (link above).
- Test presign endpoint live: https://vendr-staging-api.vendr.com/test-presign (returns example manifest JSON with sha256, timestamp, token_id).
- We will write manifests to the staging S3 bucket and enable object-lock-style retention for 90 days; we will also forward minimal audit events to your webhook if you send an HTTPS endpoint.

Timeline: canary 2026-07-02, full migration 2026-07-06. I'll create a short runbook and paste into SEC-874 by EOD.

Emily
